subject: Post-event ROI — FieldLab Summit: lead handoff discrepancy
messages:
From: FieldLab Events <events@fieldlab.co>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 16:22:00 -0000
Subject: FieldLab Summit — leads dump & pipeline questions

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for sponsoring the FieldLab Summit last week. Our events team exported the post-show lead file and attached it here (fieldlab_leads_20270309.csv). On our side the CSV shows 1,142 booth scans and 264 MQLs attributed to Redwood Inference. Your team’s pipeline report only surfaced ~240 MQLs.

Can you confirm whether you received the same lead payload? We want to avoid double-counting and make sure any co-marketing pipeline credit aligns with the SOW. Sophie from BrightBridge (our channel partner) is looping in QA to reconcile timestamps.

Attachments: fieldlab_leads_20270309.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)

Thanks,
— Devon Ellis
FieldLab Events, Partnerships
From: alex_martinez@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: FieldLab Events <events@fieldlab.co>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 09:08:00 -0000
Subject: Re: FieldLab Summit — leads dump & pipeline questions

Team — looping you in to triage. Devon says their CSV shows 264 MQLs but our pipeline shows ~240. I attached their file to this thread. Can we do a quick match against HubSpot exports and the inbound webhook logs? Key asks: 1) canonical matching fields (email vs. phone), 2) timestamp windows (timezone normalization), 3) UTM mapping for campaign=fieldlab_summit.

Marissa — can you run a first-pass match and note causes for any unmatched leads? Ben — can you check the ingestion logs (we had a small webhook retry window on Mar 9) for dropped payloads.

I propose a short mutual action plan:
- By EOD Thu: internal match summary + unmatched sample (20 rows)
- Fri 10:00 PT: 30-minute call with FieldLab & BrightBridge to review
- Monday: joint credit allocation proposal (per SOW)

Devon/Sophie — thanks for the CSV. We’ll get back with a reconciliation summary before the call.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: FieldLab Events <events@fieldlab.co>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 14:36:00 -0000
Subject: Re: FieldLab Summit — leads dump & pipeline questions

Alex/Ben/Devon — quick pass from my side. I matched FieldLab’s 264 MQLs to our HubSpot export and found: 178 exact email matches, 64 fuzzy matches (same company + phone/email mismatch), and 22 rows with no corresponding HubSpot contact or lead. I’m attaching the work file (match_analysis_20270311.xlsx) with a sample of the 22 unmatched rows and the 64 fuzzy rows with suggested normalization.

Observations:
- 12 of the unmatched rows appear to be job-title-only scans (no email captured) — these won’t ingest as MQLs into HubSpot by our current rules.
- 6 seem to have an extra whitespace/encoding issue (unicode non-breaking space) in the email field — lost during parsing.
- 4 are duplicates flagged by our dedupe policy (we collapse on email + company within 48h).

Suggested next steps:
1) For the 12 no-email rows: ask FieldLab for a follow-up permission-to-contact flow (their badge scanner captured phone-only).
2) For encoding/whitespace rows: Ben to pull raw webhook payloads and we’ll attempt a sanitized re-import if present.
3) For duplicates: show sample IDs to FieldLab to confirm if they want split credit or consolidation (SOW prefers de-duped attribution).

Tentative credit proposal (pre-call): Redwood takes 60% of net-sourced pipeline from matched emails, FieldLab/BrightBridge split remaining 40% across channel-referral rows. I’ll mark this as proposed in the spreadsheet.

Attachments: match_analysis_20270311.xlsx (XLSX, 420KB)

—Marissa
Director, Field Marketing, Redwood Inference
From: Sophie Kent <sophie.kent@brightbridge.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: FieldLab Events <events@fieldlab.co>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 19:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: FieldLab Summit — leads dump & pipeline questions

Appreciate the breakdown Marissa — Sophie from BrightBridge here. Our channel ops disagree with the 60/40 framing; their downstream opportunity records show a higher conversion from the 64 fuzzy matches (we have traced several to direct demos booked). For contract clarity: SOW FD-3981, Section 3.2 states co-marketing credit should be based on raw lead ownership at capture unless explicitly resolved by joint verification.

Could you please provide the raw timestamped lead dump (badge timestamp + capture method) for the 264 rows so we can run a time-of-capture parity check? If Redwood needs re-imports to reflect the 12 no-email rows, BrightBridge is willing to support enrichment via our data ops vendor but we need to agree on whether that changes baseline credit percentages.

We’re available for the Fri 10:00 PT slot but request the raw dump before the call.

—Sophie Kent
Channel Ops Lead, BrightBridge
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: FieldLab Events <events@fieldlab.co>, Sophie Kent <sophie.kent@brightbridge.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 09:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: FieldLab Summit — leads dump & pipeline questions

All — I pulled the raw webhook logs and the badge timestamps from our ingestion buckets. Attached are two artifacts: a filtered raw dump (raw_webhooks_20270309.jsonl) and a timestamp parity sample (timestamp_pairing_20270314.csv). I flagged 18 webhook retries that occurred during the 09:15–09:45 PT window on Mar 9 — those correspond to 9 of the 22 unmatched rows. I’ve also sanitized the 6 whitespace/encoding emails and prepared a candidate re-import file (candidate_reimport_20270314.csv).

Proposed immediate actions:
- Re-import sanitized rows for the 6 suspected encoding misses (no policy change required)
- FieldLab to run enrichment on the 12 phone-only captures and share permission confirmations
- Joint decision on duplicate rows: if FieldLab confirms duplicates were independent individuals, split credit 50/50 for those converted opps; otherwise Redwood applies de-dupe per SOW.

If that plan looks good, I’ll push the sanitized re-import Monday morning (will record change events and keep the original raw entries for audit). Planning the Fri call for record — but we can also do a follow-up Mon to confirm the re-import results.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Sales Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
